claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 is in a hierarchical-heterostructured state featuring multilevel chemical fluctuations.
A novel interatomic potential can be specifically designed to capture interactions within the hierarchical heterostructure of HfNbTiVAl10.
Applying the novel interatomic potential will improve the accuracy of predicted Young's modulus.
Applying the novel interatomic potential will improve the accuracy of predicted yield strength.
Applying the novel interatomic potential will improve the accuracy of predicted toughness.
Applying the novel interatomic potential will improve computational efficiency relative to the listed current computational methods.
Thermophysical-parameter calculations, CALPHAD, first-principles calculations, and machine-learning modeling constitute the comparison baseline.
The potential will cease to be reliable if the material structure deviates significantly from the hierarchical heterostructure.
The potential will cease to be reliable when tensile or fracture conditions fall outside its validated range.
A blinded prospective benchmark will compare the potential with current methods using Young's modulus, yield strength, toughness, and computational time.
Failure to improve predictive accuracy or computational efficiency by more than approximately 10% will falsify the hypothesis.
